title: Full Broadway Review: @theatreislife I can’t get over how much faster...
transcript: Y'all have to talk about 1776. I know I have not posted a single review yet for my New York trip. I promise they are coming. But I am literally still in the parking lot at the Denver Center, and I feel an addendum to the show must be made. I originally saw the show in previews on Broadway, and if you recall, I hated this production. And I don't say that lightly. It is very rare for me to just outright hate a show. And y'all, I have to take all of that back because I just saw on tour, and I loved it. I honestly wasn't even gonna see it on tour, but word of mouth is a powerful thing, and everybody that I know that saw it later in the run or on tour really enjoyed it, and so I figured, why not? And there have been other examples of me seeing something on Broadway, not liking it, and then really liking it on tour. It is also Transgender Day of visibility, and when shit is going down in the world and I feel frustrated, the thing that I like to do is go to a theater. I also follow a lot of the people in this cast. I think they're super talented, so I wanted to support them. So I figured, why not? We'll give it another shot. It was worth it. I was really glad I revisited this show. The show is a lot tighter than It was on Broadway. The pacing was a lot faster. It ran about 8 minutes faster by comparing my curtain call pictures. I don't know if the intermissions were longer or not, but that's a lot faster. Everybody seemed like they were performing the same show. When I originally saw it on Broadway, it felt like some people were really going for the accent and some weren't. And it felt like some people were in a comedy and some were in a drama. It felt like totally the entire show is very consistent. It had those comedic moments, it had those dramatic moments, but everyone was on the same page throughout the show. You can also tell that a lot of this cast has performed together for a very long time now. They all really worked well with each other. The sound mixing was a lot better, which is actually surprising, because usually I hate the sound in the Denver Center, but it was really good today. And I really appreciated what they were doing with the orchestrations more. It sounded a lot smoother and you could hear the vocals a lot better. After seeing it tonight, I actually really wanna cast recording for this because there are some stunning orchestrations in here. And overall, the moments that I felt when I saw it on Broadway were talking down to an audience more. Felt like they were bringing the audience into a story. And these were small changes, just nuances. In the performances, that helped certain things to land better for me. Moments like the demigod lines, I felt landed a lot better. Even the costume changes that happened throughout the show, I felt were done a lot more subtly, and so it was something to notice, as opposed to, hey, notice me doing this thing with my coat? I lost a clip somewhere, so you get this of me literally in the parking lot without the background. But one of the things that I think also helped is that now, even though there were still a couple things for me that didn't quite work because I was expecting them, this time they bugged me a lot less, and I was able to see past them and see, like, the things that ultimately did work. Like, I still don't feel like the intermission is in the right place. It feels like they're putting that intermission there just so that one of the actresses can have a costume change, but it ultimately feels out of place. The egg is supposed to be in usually the act 2 opener, and I feel like it just works better as an act 2 opener. I also don't quite feel like the egg Powerpoint quite nails it for me, but I do really love those orchestration, so you know, it's 5050. Same with the barrels at the end of the show. I feel like it's kind of unnecessary, but now that I know it's coming, It bugged me a lot less though. I think that the ending is haunting enough even if you just have the costume change without the barrel reveal. Which really isn't a spoiler. But yeah, the revival works a lot better for me now, and if you get a chance to see it on tour, I actually recommend it.
